_expect.name: Archangel Valley Sport and Traditional Climbing

ak_archangel_valley_sport_and_traditiona.blurb: Archangel Valley is the main climbing zone of Hatcher Pass, in Alaska's south central region, reached by driving north of Anchorage through Palmer. The rock is blocky granite, mossy in places because spring and fall bring steady rain. Traditional climbing leads the way, with a smaller share of sport routes, boulder problems and a few alpine lines. Roped climbs run from 5.7 to 5.13, with the thickest cluster around 5.10 and 5.11 and only a handful at 5.12 and above; the boulders run from V0 to V4. The walls are spread across the valley, including the Monolith area, Green Gully, the Diamond and Zulu Wall.

nh_town_forest_south.blurb: Town Forest South is a bouldering-only zone in the woods outside Exeter, New Hampshire, in the seacoast region. The boulders are scattered through forest on the south side of the highway that cuts the town's boulder woods in two, with most of the problems on the western half. Easy and moderate lines make up the bulk, V0 to V3, with a solid middle at V4 and V5 and a thin top end reaching about V8. Clusters such as Cthulhu Boulders, The Shire and Fort Rock hold the most problems, while many smaller blocks carry just a few each.

tn_deep_creek.blurb: Deep Creek is a sport-climbing venue in the Chattanooga area of Tennessee, where cliffs line a boulder-strewn creek beneath old hemlocks. The sandstone is steep and powerful, with routes that tend to be thuggy on mostly good holds. Almost everything is bolted, and the grades skew hard: the bulk sit at 5.11 and 5.12, with a smaller group at 5.10 and below and a few 5.13s. Main Wall carries the most routes and the highest concentration of classics, while Tea and Crumpets Wall, Creekside and the Hemlock Block add variety. Some lines seep at the top in winter and spring, though parts of Main Wall are nearly always dry, and the north-facing Hemlock Block offers shade for summer days.

az_euro_dog_valley.blurb: Euro Dog Valley is a side valley of Queen Creek Canyon in central Arizona, above the town of Superior and roughly an hour east of the Phoenix metro area, with a seasonal creek running through it. The canyon's rock is volcanic tuff. Bouldering is the main draw, with groups such as Scatterbrain Boulder, Cattleguard Boulders, Mermaid Lagoon and Peter Pan Playground. Problems run from easy to very hard, but V0 to V5 holds most of them. A smaller set of sport routes, mostly 5.9 to 5.12 and peaking at 5.10, hangs on walls like Yakov Wall and Hook Wall, along with a few top-ropes and trad lines.

bc_evergreen_drive_crags.blurb: The Evergreen Drive Crags make up the north end of Skaha Bluffs, just outside Penticton in British Columbia's Okanagan. Short trails link one wall to the next: Canoe Buttress sits closest and faces east, Foreplay climbs higher on a hill and catches the late-day sun, and Behemoth lies beyond with a run of bluffs. Nearly everything is sport, with a small amount of trad. Grades centre on 5.10, with plenty of 5.11, a decent number of 5.9 and easier routes, a smaller band of 5.12 and a few 5.13s. The Canoe Trail Crags work well as an after-work stop, sunny early and shaded later, and poison ivy lines some of the trails.

co_eldorado_canyon_bouldering.blurb: Eldorado Canyon Bouldering gathers the boulders of Eldorado Canyon State Park, in the Front Range southwest of Boulder, Colorado. The stone is polished sandstone, firm and clean, which gives many clear, obvious lines. Difficulty covers the full range from V0 to V11, with most problems between V1 and V6 and a real hard tail above that. Bigger clusters include East Draw, West World, the Musical Boulders and the Gill Boulder, and plenty of other blocks hold only a few problems each. Many of the canyon's boulders are undocumented, so exploring pays off. Summers in the canyon are very hot and the rock can feel slick, while winter conditions are inconsistent.
